_comment: cbom-js detection registry. Every crypto asset, pattern, and rule lives here. Add a new library by adding an entry — no code changes needed.

createCipher.notes: createCipher is deprecated — use createCipheriv instead

createDecipher.notes: createDecipher is deprecated — use createDecipheriv instead

jsonwebtoken.description: JSON Web Token signing and verification

hash.notes: bcrypt — secure adaptive password hashing KDF

hashSync.notes: bcrypt — secure adaptive password hashing KDF

argon2.description: Argon2 password hashing (winner of Password Hashing Competition)

hash.notes: Argon2 — memory-hard KDF, recommended for new password hashing

tweetnacl.description: Port of TweetNaCl — public-domain crypto library

libsodium-wrappers.description: libsodium JS wrapper — modern crypto primitives

@noble/hashes.description: Audited and minimal JS implementations of hash functions

@noble/curves.description: Audited elliptic curves — P256, P384, secp256k1, Ed25519

JSEncrypt.notes: JSEncrypt — RSA PKCS#1v1.5, consider using OAEP padding instead

ModeOfOperation.ecb.notes: ECB mode — does not provide semantic security, leaks data patterns

sha.js.description: SHA hash functions in pure JavaScript

v1.notes: uuid v1 is time-based — not suitable for security-sensitive identifiers

Strategy.notes: Local strategy — verify password hashing implementation separately

Microsoft.AspNetCore.DataProtection.description: ASP.NET Core Data Protection and Identity crypto APIs

methods.name: PasswordHasher
methods.notes: ASP.NET Core Identity PasswordHasher uses PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256

webcrypto-subtle.description: Web Crypto API (SubtleCrypto) — browser and Node.js standard crypto interface
webcrypto-subtle.notes: crypto.subtle.<method>(algorithm, ...). Algorithm is either a string or an object whose 'name' property carries the algorithm. Detection reads algoFromOption 'name' first, falling back to algoArgIndex 0 when the argument is a plain string literal.

importKey.notes: subtle.importKey(format, keyData, algorithm, ...) — algorithm is the 3rd positional arg

wrapKey.notes: subtle.wrapKey(format, key, wrappingKey, wrapAlgo) — wrap algorithm is the 4th positional arg

algorithms._comment: Algorithm metadata — severity, quantum safety, CWEs, primitive, cryptoFunctions, classicalSecurityLevel, OID. Every field used by cbomGenerator. No hardcoding needed in code.

DES-ECB.notes: DES-ECB is broken — weak key and ECB mode both apply

SHA256withRSA.notes: RSA-PKCS1v1.5 with SHA-256 — consider RSA-PSS for new code

SHA256withRSAandMGF1.notes: RSA-PSS with SHA-256 — preferred over PKCS1v1.5

MD5withRSA.notes: MD5withRSA is broken — MD5 is cryptographically compromised

SHA1withRSA.notes: SHA-1 is cryptographically weak — migrate to SHA-256 or higher

SHA1withECDSA.notes: SHA-1 with ECDSA is weak — upgrade to SHA-256

ED25519.notes: Ed25519 — quantum vulnerable but strong classically

EDDSA.notes: EdDSA — quantum vulnerable but strong classically

MGF1.notes: MGF1 — mask generation function used in RSA-PSS and OAEP

CONCATENATIONKDF.notes: Concatenation KDF — used in ECDH-ES key derivation (JOSE/JWK)

RAW.notes: RAW key format — used in SecretKeySpec construction

HMACSHA2.notes: HMAC-SHA2 family — used in AES-CBC-HMAC-SHA2 JWE encryption

EVP-KDF.notes: EVP KDF is an OpenSSL legacy KDF — prefer PBKDF2, scrypt, or Argon2

UUID-V1.notes: UUID v1 is time-based — predictable, not suitable for secrets

INSECURE-RANDOM.notes: java.util.Random is not cryptographically secure. Use java.security.SecureRandom instead.

SSL-2.0.notes: SSLv2 is completely broken and must not be used

SSL-3.0.notes: SSLv3 is vulnerable to POODLE attack

NONE.notes: JWT algorithm=none disables signature verification entirely

DYNAMIC-ALGO.notes: Algorithm value is dynamic — could not be resolved statically

PKCS12.notes: PKCS#12 keystore format — preferred over legacy JKS

JKS.notes: JKS uses proprietary encryption and weak SHA-1 integrity — migrate to PKCS12

JCEKS.notes: JCEKS is a stronger Sun extension of JKS but still not preferred over PKCS12

AES-256-CBC-HMAC-SHA256.notes: ASP.NET Core Data Protection composite authenticated encryption

ML-KEM-512.notes: ML-KEM (FIPS 203, formerly Kyber-512) — NIST-standardized post-quantum KEM, Category 1

ML-KEM-768.notes: ML-KEM (FIPS 203, formerly Kyber-768) — NIST-standardized post-quantum KEM, Category 3

ML-KEM-1024.notes: ML-KEM (FIPS 203, formerly Kyber-1024) — NIST-standardized post-quantum KEM, Category 5

KYBER.notes: Kyber — pre-standardization name for ML-KEM (FIPS 203). Prefer ML-KEM naming for new code.

ML-DSA-44.notes: ML-DSA (FIPS 204, formerly Dilithium2) — NIST-standardized post-quantum signature, Category 2

ML-DSA-65.notes: ML-DSA (FIPS 204, formerly Dilithium3) — NIST-standardized post-quantum signature, Category 3

ML-DSA-87.notes: ML-DSA (FIPS 204, formerly Dilithium5) — NIST-standardized post-quantum signature, Category 5

DILITHIUM.notes: Dilithium — pre-standardization name for ML-DSA (FIPS 204). Prefer ML-DSA naming for new code.

SLH-DSA-SHA2-128S.notes: SLH-DSA (FIPS 205, formerly SPHINCS+) — stateless hash-based signature, small-signature variant

SLH-DSA-SHA2-128F.notes: SLH-DSA (FIPS 205, formerly SPHINCS+) — stateless hash-based signature, fast variant

SLH-DSA-SHA2-192S.notes: SLH-DSA (FIPS 205, formerly SPHINCS+) — Category 3, small-signature variant

SLH-DSA-SHA2-256S.notes: SLH-DSA (FIPS 205, formerly SPHINCS+) — Category 5, small-signature variant

SPHINCS+.notes: SPHINCS+ — pre-standardization name for SLH-DSA (FIPS 205). Prefer SLH-DSA naming for new code.

FN-DSA.notes: FN-DSA (FIPS 206 draft, formerly Falcon) — lattice-based signature, not yet finalized

FALCON.notes: Falcon — pre-standardization name for FN-DSA (FIPS 206 draft).

XMSS.notes: XMSS (RFC 8391) — stateful hash-based signature. Quantum-safe but stateful: key reuse across states is catastrophic. Verify state management.

LMS.notes: LMS (RFC 8554) — stateful hash-based signature. Quantum-safe but stateful: key/state reuse is catastrophic. Verify state management.

RSASSA-PKCS1-V1_5.notes: WebCrypto RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5 — legacy padding, prefer RSA-PSS for new code

hardcodedPatterns._comment: Variable name patterns that suggest a hardcoded secret. Tool flags when these variables are assigned string literals.

insecureRandomPatterns._comment: Patterns for detecting non-cryptographic randomness used in security contexts

patterns.notes: Math.random() is not cryptographically secure. Use crypto.randomBytes() instead
Date.now() is predictable — must not be used as cryptographic entropy

tlsPatterns._comment: TLS/HTTPS property names and values to detect in object configurations
